title: LLM Controls and APIs
tagline: Tokens, knobs and APIs: what you can control, and what the model quietly rejects.
story: The question reaches the model. Before it answers, the request is cut into tokens, fitted into a window and shaped by controls that differ by vendor and by model family. Pick wrongly and you get half an answer, a 400 on a parameter that used to work, a bill that jumps at a hidden threshold or state you cannot delete.
oneLiner: Learn the dials on the model itself, then choose the API, state model and knowledge strategy that survive production.
youWillLearn: Budget tokens across input, output and reasoning, and count them on the model you will actually call
Choose between temperature, top_p, seed, penalties, logit_bias, logprobs and stop, and know which a reasoning model rejects
Set reasoning effort, and decide between a bigger model, more effort, a router or a cascade
Pick structured outputs, JSON mode or strict function calling, and know the schema limits per platform
Compare Chat Completions, Responses and Anthropic Messages on state ownership, tools, portability and retention
Decide between long context, RAG, cache-augmented generation and fine-tuning (LoRA, distillation) for a given corpus

flashcards.front: What three things share one context window?
flashcards.back: Input tokens, visible output tokens and reasoning (thinking) tokens. Input and output also have separate caps, so check both.

flashcards.front: Does `max_output_tokens` reserve tokens for the answer?
flashcards.back: No. It is a ceiling and it includes reasoning tokens. A low cap can return `status: incomplete` before any visible text appears.

flashcards.front: How much headroom do OpenAI and Azure advise when you first use a reasoning model?
flashcards.back: Reserve at least 25,000 tokens for reasoning and output, then tune after you measure `reasoning_tokens` in the usage object.

flashcards.front: Why recount tokens when you move a prompt to Claude Opus 4.7 or later?
flashcards.back: Tokenizers differ. Anthropic says the newer tokenizer gives roughly 30% more tokens for the same text, depending on content.

flashcards.front: On GPT-6 models, what happens to the price above 272K input tokens?
flashcards.back: The whole request costs 2x the input and cache rates and 1.5x the output rate, not only the tokens above 272K.

flashcards.front: Name two things a `characters / 4` estimate gets wrong.
flashcards.back: Images and files, and tool definitions. Use a vendor count endpoint such as `POST /v1/responses/input_tokens` before you budget near a limit.

flashcards.front: Which controls exist in Chat Completions but not in the Responses body?
flashcards.back: `seed`, `stop`, `n`, `frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty` and `logit_bias`. Neither OpenAI API has `top_k`.

flashcards.front: Is `seed` a determinism guarantee?
flashcards.back: No. It is best effort and marked Beta in Chat Completions. Log `system_fingerprint` to spot backend changes between calls.

flashcards.front: Where does `top_k` exist?
flashcards.back: Not in OpenAI bodies. Anthropic Messages deprecated it and returns 400 on models released after Opus 4.6. Gemini uses `topK` in `generationConfig`.

flashcards.front: What sampling values do Claude models released after Opus 4.6 accept?
flashcards.back: Only temperature 1.0 and top_p of 0.99 or higher. Any other value returns HTTP 400.

flashcards.front: What does OpenAI say to remove when reasoning effort is not `none`?
flashcards.back: `temperature`, `top_p` and `top_logprobs`, plus `logprobs` in Chat. Azure's page lists more as rejected, so test your deployment.

flashcards.front: Which max-token parameter belongs to which API?
flashcards.back: `max_completion_tokens` for Chat, `max_output_tokens` for Responses, `max_tokens` for Anthropic (required). All three include reasoning or thinking tokens.

flashcards.front: What does `logit_bias` take?
flashcards.back: A map from token id to a bias between -100 and 100, in Chat Completions only. Values between -1 and 1 are the usual range.

flashcards.front: Which effort values does GPT-6 Astra accept?
flashcards.back: `low` to `max`. `none` returns HTTP 400. GPT-6.1 Sol also drops `minimal`, while GPT-6 Sol and Luna accept `none`.

flashcards.front: How do you set effort and thinking on Anthropic?
flashcards.back: `output_config.effort` takes `low` to `max`, and `thinking` is `adaptive`. Manual `budget_tokens` is not accepted on the newest models.

flashcards.front: JSON mode versus structured outputs?
flashcards.back: JSON mode only guarantees valid JSON. Structured outputs (`json_schema` with `strict: true`) guarantee the schema.

flashcards.front: Name three OpenAI strict-schema rules.
flashcards.back: Every field required (use a union with `null` for optional), `additionalProperties: false`, and an object root. Limits are 5,000 properties and 10 nesting levels.

flashcards.front: How do Azure structured output limits differ from OpenAI's?
flashcards.back: Azure allows up to 100 properties and 5 nesting levels, and lists `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern` and `format` as unsupported. Read the Azure page for Azure.

flashcards.front: What breaks when you use Chat Completions with tools and reasoning on GPT-5.4 or later?
flashcards.back: Chat Completions does not support tool calling when `reasoning_effort` is not `none`. Use Responses.

flashcards.front: What is an Item in the Responses API?
flashcards.back: A typed unit such as `message`, `reasoning`, `function_call` or `function_call_output`. `output` can hold several, so never assume text sits at index 0.

flashcards.front: Three ways to hold conversation state with OpenAI?
flashcards.back: Replay history yourself, chain with `previous_response_id`, or use the Conversations API, which is durable (no 30 day TTL) but not ZDR eligible.

flashcards.front: What does `previous_response_id` cost you?
flashcards.back: Earlier input tokens bill again on every turn, responses expire after 30 days and top-level `instructions` are not carried over.

flashcards.front: How does stateless mode work for reasoning models?
flashcards.back: With `store` false or ZDR, reasoning items carry `encrypted_content`. You replay every output item, encrypted reasoning included.

flashcards.front: Does `store: false` mean nothing is kept?
flashcards.back: No. Abuse monitoring logs can keep content up to 30 days unless ZDR or Modified Abuse Monitoring applies.

flashcards.front: What happened to the OpenAI Assistants API?
flashcards.back: Announced 2025-08-26, sunset 2026-08-26. Threads map to Conversations, Runs to Responses. Azure docs give the same date and point to Foundry Agent Service.

flashcards.front: Is Anthropic Messages stateful?
flashcards.back: No. `POST /v1/messages` is stateless, so you send the full history every call. `max_tokens` is required and `stop_reason` replaces `finish_reason`.

flashcards.front: When does Anthropic say you can skip RAG?
flashcards.back: For a knowledge base under about 200,000 tokens (about 500 pages, an estimate): put it in the prompt and use prompt caching.

flashcards.front: Why is fine-tuning a weak way to add facts?
flashcards.back: Ovadia et al. found RAG beat unsupervised fine-tuning. Gekhman et al. found new facts are learned slowly and, once learned, raise hallucination.

flashcards.front: What does LoRA change in a model?
flashcards.back: It freezes the base weights and trains low-rank matrices. Against full Adam fine-tuning of GPT-3 175B: 10,000x fewer trainable parameters, 3x less GPU memory, no added inference latency.

flashcards.front: What is distillation?
flashcards.back: Training a small model on a large model's outputs (Hinton et al., 2015). OpenAI's pattern: tune the prompt on a large model, then fine-tune a smaller one on its outputs.

flashcards.front: What are the Azure model router modes?
flashcards.back: Balanced (default, cheapest model within about 1% to 2% of top quality), Cost (about 5% to 6%) and Quality. The window is the smallest in the pool.

flashcards.front: What does batch processing give you, and what does it cost?
flashcards.back: 50% off on OpenAI, Azure and Anthropic, with a 24 hour window. It is offline only, and OpenAI batches are not ZDR eligible.

glossary.def: The unit a model reads and writes. A token is usually a word piece, not a word. Counts differ by tokenizer, so always count on the model you call.
The total tokens a model can hold in one request. Input, visible output and reasoning tokens share it, and input and output also carry separate caps.
Hidden thinking tokens. They are billed as output, count against the window and the output cap, and appear in usage details.
Sample only from the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability reaches `p`.
Log probabilities of the generated tokens and their top alternatives. Useful as a confidence signal for classification.
A decoding mode that constrains output to a JSON schema (`strict: true`). JSON mode only guarantees syntactically valid JSON.
The typed unit of the Responses API: `message`, `reasoning`, `function_call`, `function_call_output` and others.
Zero data retention. An account-level control that forces `store` to false and limits which endpoints you may use.
Shrinking a long conversation by summarizing or encrypting earlier turns. OpenAI offers client-side `/responses/compact` and server-side `context_management`.
Preload a small, stable corpus into a long context and reuse its cached state instead of retrieving per question.
Low-rank adaptation. Freeze the base weights and train small low-rank matrices, which cuts trainable parameters and memory.
Train a small model to imitate a large model's outputs to keep most of the behaviour at lower cost.
A service that picks a model per request. Azure's version has Balanced, Cost and Quality modes and failover.
Try a small model first and escalate to a larger one when a check fails, such as an invalid schema or low confidence.

claims.text: GPT-6 models list a 1,050,000 token context window, 922,000 max input tokens and 128,000 max output tokens.
On GPT-6 models, prompts over 272K input tokens cost 2x the input and cache rates and 1.5x the output rate for the whole request.
On Azure, a standard gpt-4.1 deployment allows 300,000 tokens of context although the model supports 1,047,576.
Claude Opus 4.7 and later use a tokenizer that gives roughly 30% more tokens for the same text, depending on content.
OpenAI and Azure advise reserving at least 25,000 tokens for reasoning and output when starting out with a reasoning model.
The Responses body has no seed, stop, n, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, logit_bias or top_k.
Chat Completions seed is marked Beta and best effort, and stop accepts up to 4 sequences and is not supported on o3 and o4-mini.
Claude models released after Opus 4.6 accept only temperature 1.0 and top_p of 0.99 or higher, return 400 for other values, and reject top_k.
OpenAI says to remove temperature, top_p and top_logprobs when reasoning effort is not none, and logprobs too in Chat.
Anthropic's OpenAI SDK compatibility layer silently ignores seed, logprobs, penalties, logit_bias, response_format, reasoning_effort, store and strict.
GPT-6 Astra rejects reasoning effort none with HTTP 400, and GPT-6.1 Sol accepts neither none nor minimal.
Claude output_config.effort takes low, medium, high, xhigh and max.
Default effort for Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 is high, medium, high and medium respectively.

Azure model router Balanced mode picks the cheapest model within about 1% to 2% of top quality, runs only on Global Standard and Data Zone Standard, and its effective window is the smallest in the pool.
OpenAI Batch gives a 50% discount with completion_window 24h, up to 50,000 requests and 200 MB per file.
OpenAI structured outputs allow up to 5,000 object properties and 10 nesting levels, and strict mode needs every field required and additionalProperties false.
Azure structured outputs allow up to 100 object properties and 5 nesting levels and list minLength, maxLength, pattern and format as unsupported.
From GPT-5.4, Chat Completions does not support tool calling when reasoning_effort is not none.
Claude tool_choice any and tool return 400 on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1.
Responses are stored by default for 30 days, previous_response_id bills earlier input tokens again and does not carry over top-level instructions.
The Conversations API, released 2025-08-20, is not ZDR eligible, and ZDR-eligible endpoints include chat completions and responses.
OpenAI announced Assistants deprecation on 2025-08-26 and sunset the API on 2026-08-26, mapping Threads to Conversations and Runs to Responses.
Azure OpenAI v1 API uses a base URL ending /openai/v1 and needs no api-version.
NoLiMa found that at 32K, 11 of 13 models claiming 128K or more fell below 50% of their short-context baseline.
Anthropic says a knowledge base under about 200,000 tokens can go in the prompt, and contextual retrieval cut failed retrievals by 49%, or 67% with reranking.
OpenAI's fine-tuning notice is dated 2026-05-07, and on 2027-01-06 active customers can no longer create jobs.
LoRA cut trainable parameters 10,000x and GPU memory 3x against full Adam fine-tuning of GPT-3 175B with no added inference latency.
OpenAI gives at least 6 months of notice for GA models and Anthropic at least 60 days for publicly released models.
